title: Scope

paras.text: The institutions in question are the following, further to the exercise of a regulated activity:

a) credit institutions governed by Belgian law as referred to in Article 1 §3, first paragraph, of the Act of 25 April 2014 on the legal status and supervision of credit institutions and stockbroking firms; b) Belgian branches of credit institutions as referred to in Article 1 §3, first paragraph, of the aforementioned act, governed by the law of another Member State or of a non-EEA country;

c) credit institutions as referred to in Article 1 §3, first paragraph, of the aforementioned act, governed by the law of another Member State which rely on a tied agent established in Belgium in order to perform investment services and/or activities within the meaning of Article 2(1) of the Act of 25 October 2016 on access to the activity of investment services and on the legal status and supervision of portfolio management and investment advisory firms as well as ancillary services within the meaning of Article 2(2) of the same act in Belgium; d) credit institutions as referred to in Article 1 §3, first paragraph, of the aforementioned act, governed by the law of another Member State which rely on an agent established in Belgium to provide services in the country, consisting of receiving deposits or other repayable funds within the meaning of Article 4(1) of the same act;

a) insurance companies governed by Belgian law as referred to in Book II of the Act of 13 March 2016 on the legal status and supervision of insurance and reinsurance companies, authorised to engage in the life insurance activities referred to in Annex II of the same act; b) Belgian branches of insurance companies governed by the law of another Member State or of a non-EEA country, as referred to, respectively, in Articles 550 and 584 of the same act, which are authorised to engage in the life insurance activities referred to in Annex II of the same act in Belgium;

a) payment institutions governed by Belgian law as referred to in Book 2, Chapter 1, Title 2 of the Act of 21 December 2009 on the legal status of payment institutions and electronic money institutions, access to the activity of payment service provider, access to the activity of issuing electronic money, and access to payment systems; b) branches in Belgium of payment institutions governed by the law of another Member State or of a non-EEA country, as referred to, respectively, in Articles 39 and 46 of the same act; c) payment institutions granted an exemption under Article 48 of the same act; d) payment institutions as referred to in Article 4(4) of Directive 2015/2366/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 November 2015 on payment services in the internal market, amending Directives 2002/65/EC, 2009/110/EC and 2013/36/EU and Regulation (EU) No 1093/2010, and repealing Directive 2007/64/EC, governed by the law of another Member State and offering payment services in Belgium through one or more persons established in Belgium who represent the institution for that purpose;

a) electronic money issuers as referred to in Article 59(4) and (5) of the aforementioned Act of 21 December 2009; b) electronic money institutions governed by Belgian law as referred to in Book 3, Chapter 1, Title 2, of the same act; c) branches in Belgium of electronic money institutions governed by the law of another Member State or of a third country as referred to, respectively, in Article 91 and in Book 3, Chapter 3, Title 2 of the same act; d) electronic money institutions granted an exemption under Article 105 of the same act; e) electronic money institutions as referred to in Article 2(1) of Directive 2009/110/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 September 2009 on the taking up, pursuit and prudential supervision of the business of electronic money institutions amending Directives 2005/60/EC and 2006/48/EC and repealing Directive 2000/46/EC, governed by the law of another Member State and distributing electronic money in Belgium through one or more persons established in Belgium who represent the institution for that purpose;
central securities depositories as defined in Article 36/26/1 of the Act of 22 February 1998 establishing the organic statute of the National Bank of Belgium;
mutual guarantee societies as referred to in the Royal Decree of 30 April 1999 on the legal status and supervision of mutual guarantee societies;

a) stockbroking firms as referred to in Article 1 §3, second paragraph, of the Act of 25 April 2014 on the legal status and supervision of credit institutions and stockbroking firms governed by Belgian law; b) Belgian branches of stockbroking firms as referred to in Article 1 §3, second paragraph, of the same act, governed by the law of another Member State or of a non-EEA country; c) stockbroking firms as referred to in Article 1 §3, second paragraph, of the same act, governed by the law of another Member State and relying on a tied agent established in Belgium in order to perform investment services and/or activities within the meaning of Article 2(1) of the Act of 25 October 2016 on access to the activity of investment services and on the legal status and supervision of portfolio management and investment advisory firms as well as ancillary services within the meaning of Article 2(2) of the same act in Belgium.
For financial institutions, the applicability of the AML Act and the NBB Anti-Money Laundering Regulation and the scope of these AML/CFT webpages are determined by two factors:
the nature of the professional activity exercised by the entity concerned;
the presence of an establishment on the Belgian territory .

It follows from the territorial scope of application of the statutory and regulatory AML/CFT provisions that the provisions of the AML/CFT Act and the NBB Anti-Money Laundering Regulation apply to the following entities, for which these AML/CFT webpages are also intended:
financial institutions governed by Belgian law;

financial institutions governed by the law of another EEA Member State or of a non-EEA country established on the Belgian territory to offer financial services or products in Belgium, regardless of whether the establishment takes the form of: a branch; one or more tied or independent agents or distributors established in Belgium acting in the framework of an agency agreement concluded with the financial institution, which does not have another type of establishment on the Belgian territory. This covers (i) credit institutions and stockbroking firms governed by the law of another EEA Member State that rely on a tied agent established in Belgium in order to perform investment services and/or activities, (ii) credit institutions governed by the law of another EEA Member State that rely on an agent established in Belgium to provide services consisting of receiving deposits or other repayable funds, and (iii) payment institutions and electronic money institutions governed by the law of another EEA Member State or of a non-EEA country offering payment services or distributing electronic money, as the case may be, in Belgium exclusively through agents or distributors.

Financial institutions governed by the law of another EEA Member State or of a non-EEA country that offer financial services or products in Belgium without having any form of establishment in the country are however subject to the statutory and regulatory provisions of the country by whose law they are governed and of the other countries in which they have an establishment. The provisions of the AML/CFT Act and the NBB Anti-Money Laundering Regulation do not apply to them and a fortiori they are not the intended audience of this website.
For more information on the general scope of the Anti-Money Laundering Act, please consult the preparatory works (Act of 18 September 2017 and amending acts) (see “ Main reference documents ”).
